sadārum: to set in a row, put in order; of an account, to write out, list: isaddar(ma) “he shall write out”. Harper files the same forms under šaṭāru “to write”
manûm-count: to count, reckon (the verb; the noun manûm “mina” is another word): imannû(ma) “they shall count” — 3rd plural, impersonal
tadmiqtum: a favour, a kindness (from damāqum “to be good”; Harper tadmiktu “favor”): ana tadmiqtim “as a favour”; the commercial sense, an advance made on trust, is a guess from the context
nadûm-Š: Š-stem of nadûm “to throw”: to make (someone) throw down, to strip of: uštaddišu “he made him throw (it) down”
šipātum: wool (written SIG, as Harper’s glossary gives it): šipâtam (accusative; Harper šipâtu)
šamnum: oil, fat (written Ì.GIŠ, the signs NI + GIŠ): šamnam (accusative; Harper šamnu)
kanīkum: sealed receipt, sealed tablet (from kanākum “to seal”): kanīk kaspim “a sealed receipt for silver”, kanīkim (genitive); not the same word as kunukkum “seal”
egûm: to be careless, neglect (Harper: “to be careless”): itēgi(ma) “he has been negligent, and”
nikkazzum: UNCERTAIN: account, credit (Harper nikkazzu; modern editions normalise nikkassum “account, reckoning”): ana nikkazzim “to the account”, spelled ni-ik-ka-az-zi-im; the sense “account” or “credit” is not secure
qiāpum: to entrust, give in trust (Harper “to intrust”, listed under kapu): iqīp(ma) “he entrusted (the agent), and”
šikarum: beer (written KAŠ; Harper šikaru): šikarim (genitive), also as the price or rate “of beer”
abnum: stone; a stone used as a weight (written NA₄; Harper abnu): ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone”
sābītum: UNCERTAIN: the tavern-keeper, the woman who brews and sells beer (written ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA, “woman” + “wine”); the reading sābītum follows the modern editors — Harper gives only the signs
ṣarrūtum: criminals, rogues, rebels (Harper: “outlaws, rowdies, traitors”): ṣarrūtum, ṣarrūtim (plural noun, not a title)
rakāsum-N: N-stem of rakāsum “to bind”: to gather, band together, conspire (Harper “collect”): ittarkasū(ma) “they have gathered, and”
šunūti: them (masculine plural, accusative): ṣarrūtim šunūti “those criminals”
šī: she, that (feminine pronoun, as the independent word): ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA šī “that tavern-keeper”; the masculine is šū
redûm-lead: to lead, drive, bring (the verb; rēdûm “soldier” is another word; Harper “to conduct”): irdiam “she led (them) here”, with the ventive -am
nadītum: UNCERTAIN: a priestess, written ŠAL.NIN.AN (Harper aššatum NIN.AN, not normalised); read nadītum, the cloistered priestess of the code. The reading rests on the sign group and the context, not on a spelled word
gagûm: UNCERTAIN: the cloister, the walled house where nadītum priestesses lived (written MAL.GE.A; Harper leaves the signs unread): ina gagîm “in the cloister”
karānum: wine (written GEŠ.TIN.NA; Harper karânu): bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (É + GEŠ.TIN.NA)
erēbum: to enter: iterub “she has entered” (perfect; Harper I,2)
awīltum: woman, lady (feminine of awīlum; Harper awiltu): awīltam “woman” (accusative)
qalûm: to burn (Harper kalû, with his k): iqallû(ši) “they shall burn (her)”
dibtum: UNCERTAIN: credit, a loan on trust — Harper’s diptu “credit(?)”, with his own question mark: ana dibtim “on credit”
usakani: UNCERTAIN: a kind of beer, written U.SA.KA.NI (four signs Harper leaves unread; no meaning known): šikarim usakani “beer of the usakani (kind?)”
3-šu: threefold — the numeral 3 with -šu: adu 3-šu (a-du 3-šu) “three times over” (spoken form reconstructed)
6-šu: sixfold — the numeral 6 with -šu: adu 6-šu (a-du 6-šu) “six times over” (spoken form reconstructed)
-ši: her / it (3rd-person feminine singular suffix, on a verb): ukannūšima “they shall convict her”, inaddûši “they shall throw her”, iqallûši “they shall burn her”
5 BAN₂: fifty qa — the numeral 50 fused with the measure sign (five ban₂ of ten qa each; Harper “L QA”), one ligature on the stone; said ḫamšā qû (spoken form reconstructed). The qa is a measure of capacity

__broaden__.maḫārum: to face, withstand; qabal lā maḫārim “combat none can face” · to receive (silver, grain): imtaḫar “she received” (Harper I,2, maghāru “to receive”)
__broaden__.nakārum: UNCERTAIN: perhaps nakārum “to be hostile, to deny, to dispute”: only the first sign ik survives, which the editor doubts, so the form (ikkir-ma ?) and the sense are a guess; the verb is the editors’ restoration · ittakir “he denied, disowned (his merchant)”, ikkiru (with the subjunctive -u), ittakiršu “he denied him” — Harper “to dispute”
__broaden__.nīšum: raising, lifting; nīš qātim “prayer” (lifting of hands) · nīš ilim izakkarma “he shall swear the oath of the god” (nīš ilim “the raising (of the hand) to the god”)
__broaden__.pašārum: UNCERTAIN: the verb pašārum “to loosen, release”; in the merchant’s law, perhaps “to sell off, dispose of” (ana pašārim, restored by the editors as “for selling”): only pa-ša… survives, so the form and sense are a guess · ana pašārim “for trading” — Harper’s glossary pašāru I,1 “to trade”
__broaden__.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · ūmīšu “his days” (written UD-mi-šu): ūmīšu imannûma “they shall count his days”
__broaden__.ašrum: place; ana ašrišu “to its (proper) place” · ašar “where”, with a verb in the subjunctive: ašar illiku “where he went”
__broaden__.šamallûm: UNCERTAIN: the merchant’s agent, his trading assistant: šamallim (genitive, ša-ma-al-li-im), šamallû (nominative, ša-ma-al-lu-u₂); the editors print a logogram with a complement, so the syllabic spellings are a placeholder · now written with signs: ŠÀ.GAN₂.LÁ (Harper SA.GAN.LAL; modern ŠAMAN₂.LÁ), also with -šu: šamallīšu “his agent”
__broaden__.qaqqadum: head; the capital, the principal of a loan, as against its interest (written SAG.DU, “head”): ana qaqqadim “to the capital” (genitive, written with the logogram) · qaqqad kaspim “the capital of the silver”, also spelled syllabically ga-ga-ad
__broaden__.šīmum: purchase, purchase price · šīm šikarim “the price of beer” (written ŠÁM, Harper šîmu)
__broaden__.maḫīrum: market rate, price: ana maḫīrātišunu “at their rates” · maḫīr šikarim “the rate of beer” (written KI.LAM, Harper maḫiru)
__broaden__.rabûm: to be(come) great; š-stem šurbûm to make great · rabîtim (feminine genitive) “large”: ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone”
__broaden__.ṣibtum: interest (“increase”): ṣibtam; ṣibassu, ṣibtišu “its interest” · ṣibāt kaspim “the interest on the silver” (ṣibāt, construct form)
__broaden__.tamkārum: merchant (written tam-KAR §32, DAM.GÀR §40): the ransom-fronting, land-buying businessman of the code · written DAM.GÀR as a Sumerogram: tamkārum, tamkāram, tamkārim, tamkāršu
__broaden__.wašābum: to sit: ul uššab “he shall not sit” (the stone writes uš-ta-ab — a carver’s slip Harper flags) · to sit; to dwell, live: wašbat “she lives (in the cloister)” (stative)
__broaden__.adi: up to, times: adi 12-šu “twelvefold” · as a conjunction, “as long as”, with the subjunctive: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” · adu 3-šu, adu 6-šu “three times, six times (as much)” — the multiplier, spelled a-du
__broaden__.amārum: to see, examine: immarūma “they shall examine” · ītamar “he saw”, of a loss or profit “he met with”
__broaden__.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · alākišu “his going” (infinitive with -šu); illiku “(where) he went” (subjunctive -u)
__broaden__.bītum: house, temple (É) · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form, written É); bītiša “her house”
__broaden__.60: sixty — a single vertical wedge (the sexagesimal “one” of the next order); said šūši (?) “sixty” · a single vertical wedge also counts a measure: šūši qû “sixty qa” (of beer); spoken form reconstructed
